A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Spherical Voronoi research. All 16 pages of each version, including the supplementary material, are readable; matching text, equations, tables, and figures supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original function-fitting experiments, radiance and reflection reconstruction results, ablations, and efficiency measurements, including per-scene supplementary results.

after.justification: v2 retains original reconstruction experiments and adds quantitative site-count and environment-map fitting analyses.

M1.justification: The described SV parameterization, deferred rendering, near/far-field blending, probe interpolation, and accelerated evaluation remain unchanged. Equation (5) corrects an index to match the already stated softmax formulation; the PDFs do not establish a changed algorithm or implementation.

E1.justification: The seven reconstruction datasets are retained. v2 expands environment-map fitting to explicitly evaluated studio and forest environments alongside the road environment already illustrated in v1 Figures 1 and 10; this extends an existing task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained in the corresponding reconstruction and backbone comparisons. The new analyses reuse SH, SG, and SB; SH and SG already appeared in v1's environment-map comparison. Newly cited EnvGS and NeLF-Pro are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a radiance-capacity sweep over 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, and 16 sites, averaging quality and efficiency over bonsai and garden (Table 5). Section 9 adds environment-map comparisons at convergence under a stated equal parameter budget. Existing reconstruction protocols are retained; revised scores alone do not establish changed settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds a radiance-site sensitivity analysis and quantitative environment-map fitting with error visualizations, testing representation quality separately from the full reconstruction pipeline. Existing reflection-component ablations, probe-parameterization comparisons, and reflection quality-efficiency analysis remain.

E5.justification: Figure 4 retains the same 100 random-initialization fitting trials and outcome distributions. Neither version adds benchmark seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises SV PSNR from 28.57 to 28.71 on Mip-NeRF360, 34.53 to 34.58 on NeRF-Synthetic, 30.48 to 30.63 on DeepBlending, and 24.75 to 25.00 on Tanks&Temples. Corresponding per-scene and backbone-integration scores also change, with some metrics worsening. v2 Tables 5–6 add capacity and environment-fitting results. Reflection results and the principal rankings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation (5) changes the denominator's temperature from tau_k to tau_k', correctly normalizing across sites with different temperatures. This repairs the mathematical definition rather than merely changing notation. The remaining derivations are retained, with no new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central SV representation, radiance-modeling, and reflection-performance claims remain. However, Section 3.4 withdraws v1's claim to first introduce learnable light probes in differentiable rendering and instead distinguishes its explicit, reflection-direction SV probes from prior approaches.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new radiance-capacity results as saturating around 8–12 sites and motivates controlled environment fitting as isolating representation quality. The rewritten introduction removes v1's discussion of reflection models' sensitivity to normal errors and possible disadvantages when specular highlights are absent.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page pointer in the abstract and absolute training-time measurements for the site-count comparison, ranging from 21 to 47 minutes. Existing implementation descriptions, temperature bounds, probe counts, and acceleration refresh intervals are retained. The project pointer alone does not establish code availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds EnvGS and NeLF-Pro citations and uses them to qualify the novelty of learnable probes in Section 3.4. The broader related-work coverage remains stable; several other bibliography edits update publication metadata for already cited works.

P1.justification: v2 tightens the abstract and rewrites the introduction, organizing contributions into three bullets. It revises the probe-positioning paragraph and inserts an environment-fitting section into the supplementary narrative. Most method, experimental, and conclusion prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds two supplementary tables and an environment-fitting figure with rendered spheres and error maps. It enlarges and relocates the backbone-comparison table and arranges per-scene tables side by side. Most existing figures are retained, with layout adjustments and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The added capacity and controlled fitting analyses strengthen empirical support, while the corrected softmax equation and narrower novelty attribution improve accuracy. Reporting remains imperfect: v2 Table 5 gives 31.21 dB for eight sites on bonsai/garden, whereas Table 8's corresponding scores average about 31.40 dB, without an explained setting difference. This limits confidence in the added analysis but does not outweigh the modest gains.
